- Model consistently underestimates price spikes in the short term (1-3 days) after recent volatility, especially when sentiment is neutral or flat.
- Forecasts tend to lag behind true price movements by 2–5 days, particularly in upward trends; adjust for delayed reaction to news or policy shifts.
- Overshoots occur after sharp price increases (e.g., >10% in 1–2 days), leading to overcorrection; cap forecast peaks at 1.5x the recent 7-day high.
- Mean reversion bias: model over-predicts downward corrections after prolonged rallies; reduce forecast slope after 3 consecutive rising days.
- When sentiment is flat (all 0.00), model should not assume momentum; use 14-day moving average as baseline instead of 30-day forecast.
- In absence of sentiment signals, prioritize historical 7-day trend over 30-day forecast for short-term correction.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 3 consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 2–3% to avoid over-optimism.
- For price drops >10% from recent peak, model should not forecast further decline unless sentiment confirms bearish shift.
